lines.zh: 墙根走一圈，正好一炷香。
lines.en: One lap along the wall, one incense stick.
Steps must be heavy to be feared.
I walk the fence line on my rounds.
At night the wind comes from the lava.
My golden sword swings and clinks.
This round ends at the shroomlight.
I walk around the villagers' patches.
Blackstone dust coats my boot soles.
The village is quieter than yesterday.
I count the windows on my way back.
My snout points beyond the wall.
After this lap I hand over the post.
Standing so long, my legs go wooden.
I know the wind through this crack.
I tighten and loosen my grip on the hilt.
The villagers fall asleep before I do.
The lava turns over in the distance.
I am listening for strangers.
No dozing on this post.
My armor chafes at the shoulder.
No one has cried out tonight.
My golden blade has nicked an edge.
Halt, give your name first.
Hands away from your belt.
Strangers need a pass to enter.
Do you bring goods or weapons?
I have your face in mind now.
You have stood at the gate too long.
Do not touch the villagers' stalls.
Sheathe it, and you may pass.
You carry soil from the north.
I need to watch how you walk.
My armor took most of that.
I give half a step, never the post.
That landed on my bracer.
Teeth sank into my arm.
I stand; so does the village.
The smell of blood draws more.
The blade is still in my hand.
I count to three through my tusks.
Do not mind me; watch the gate.
I will wrap that wound later.
Gold? A guard may not take it.
That golden sword is bright and fine.

lines.zh: 你手里还有别的东西吗？
lines.en: Is there more in your hand?
I smell roast meat somewhere.
Do not test my duty with gold.
Speak to me when my shift ends.
This gold fits the gap in my bracer.
I only want a mouthful of hot water.
That potion looks warming.
Taking it means selling the village.
You bumped the watchtower post.
Your shoulder hit my armor.
Do not crowd me; I hold this gate.
Steady, this is the passage mouth.
I will not give up a single step.
Do not tread the ground under my feet.
Move, I must reach the far wall.
A firm bump; the armor holds.
Do not shove at the gate.
My snout met your head.
A night watchman does not discuss that.
My mate lives in this village too.
After shift I walk her home.
To wed, I need a stone room first.
She says I smell of iron rust.
The little ones must not play on the wall.
I keep watch; she brings water.
The feast would fill the whole village.
I will settle that match slowly.
My post matters more than my wedding.
Whose arrow is this one?
A blackstone block can patch the wall.
I pick up the broken blade and look.
A rope on the ground; keep it for the gate.
An empty bottle goes in the basket.
Who scattered these nails here?
Gold nuggets go to the village ledger.
I pick up a dropped shield.
I will clear this pile of shavings.
There are strange footprints on the ground.
Something moves beyond the wall.
That shadow does not belong here.
It keeps circling the fence.
I blow the bone whistle first.
No post covers that direction.
It snapped a wooden stake.
The villagers are still in the field.
I raise my blade and point.
Whoever dares touch the village gate.
It does not smell like a piglin.
I know that kind of low growl.
Come at me instead.
I have marked its position.
Hold the gate; do not chase far.
It retreats; I will not rush.
I track it along the wall.
Keep it off the shroomlight shoots.
Each time it turns, I freeze.
I hold the middle of this road.
Its breathing is getting closer.
My blade tip stays on it.
I shift in front of the villagers.
It wants to slip to the side gate.
I drop the door bar into place.
It broke the marker I left.
I press forward, one step at a time.
Is anyone watching my back?
This village is mine to hold tonight.
The golden blade lands on its shoulder.
This swing is for the door bar.
The strike throws off a hot wind.
It slams into the fence.
My fist is faster than my snout.
Shield forward; back away.
My armor caught its teeth.
I cut across its knees.
That swing struck out sparks.
Do not fall back; villagers are behind.
I drive my pommel at its snout.
Hold your ground; one more blow.
Its claw snags my bracer.
After this fight I change shifts.
I take the post, blade still in hand.
Two bricks fell from the wall.
Tonight it is my turn at the gate.
I take the first watch at the gate.
The pig village needs open eyes.
I hang my shield on the post.
The road in is worn wider again.
I check the door bar first.
I lit the watchtower lamp.
Who moved my spear last night?
Quiet village; good time to patrol.
My stretch begins right here.
The heat of the lava reaches me.
I slid down off the wall.
This water is unnaturally cold.
That blast is still ringing in my ears.
An arrow passed through my pauldron.
Something is pressing down on me.
Guarding hungry makes my eyes swim.
Lightning hit the wall, blinding bright.
I have fallen long and not landed.
